title: Prefill attention with E4M3 Q and K
formula: out = softmax(Q @ K^T / sqrt(128)) @ V per batch, float8_e4m3fn Q[B*MQ,128] and K[B*N,128], BF16 V[B*N,128] and out[B*MQ,128], FP32 online state and accumulator
study_for: The E4M3 half of a matched pair: the same schedule as `attention.a5_pfa_qk_hif8` with `float8_e4m3fn` Q/K instead of HiFloat8, and BF16 everywhere else. The two units differ in the carrier and in nothing else, which is what makes a comparison between them mean something; `attention.a5_pfa_bf16` is the unquantised baseline both are measured against.

Stream-K sharding over the flat (m_tile, k_tile) grid rather than over M tiles alone: grep `fd_accum`, `fd_max`, `fd_sum`. A core boundary that lands inside an M tile makes that tile write an unnormalised partial state to the GM workspace, and after a vec-wide barrier `fd_merge_vf` rescales the two partials onto a common row max while `output_cast_vf` does the single BF16 rounding. `fd_matched` and `fd_split` are the same shape either side of that boundary.

Why the prefix and suffix partials get their own UB tensors instead of the cycling buffer slots: grep `ub_accum_pfx`. The full pipe indexes `ub_rmax`/`ub_rsum`/`ub_accum` by `mt % CACHE`, and the auto-sync tracker cannot see the alias between a literal slot and a runtime one, so a full-pipe `init_softmax_state` would reset the row max before the prefix's workspace store had flushed. Separating the buffers removes the alias instead of adding a barrier to paper over it.

A partial K-tile is masked once, not per row: `neg_fill_rows` fills the invalid key rows of the transposed score with NEG_LARGE before the tail softmax, so they lose the lane-wise max and exponentiate to exactly zero. The arithmetic is identical to the per-row scalar clamp it replaces; what goes away is a 64-bit compare inside the vec scope, which was the whole of the tail-shape gap on the board.
do_not_copy_when: Your Q or K can be non-finite. The carriers are finite `float8_e4m3fn`: nothing in the kernel clamps or checks them, and one NaN carrier propagates through the row max into every element of that query row.

More than two cores can own one query tile. The merge reads exactly two workspace slots per split tile, so a `block_dim` that cuts one M tile three ways, or that puts two interior boundaries in the same tile, merges the wrong pair without complaining -- the recorded failure is B=1, MQ=1028, N=256 at block_dim=32. Each case here names a block_dim that satisfies the precondition; it is not a free knob.
Your head dimension is not 128. D=128 is wired into the tiling as TILE_M/TILE_N=128 and two 64-lane FP32 register chunks per output row, and is not a parameter despite being a kernel argument.
